newsitem.title: FRANCE: Credit Lyonnais sale of Creberg seen soon - source.
newsitem.headline: Credit Lyonnais sale of Creberg seen soon - source.

text.p: Continuing its asset disposal drive, French bank Credit Lyonnais is expected to sign this week a deal to sell its majority stake in Italian bank Credito Bergamasco (Creberg), a well-informed source said on Monday.
The state-controlled bank declined to comment on newspaper reports that it was in negotiations to sell the bank to Italy's Banca Popolare di Verona.
The bank holds 56.8 percent of Creberg which is based in northern Italy.

Credit Lyonnais has been under heavy pressure to sell non-French assets to meet conditions set by the European Commission for approving state aid to the bank, which almost collapsed in the early 1990s following an ill-fated expansion spree.
The bank, which has staged a strong recovery after a series of huge losses, has said it will continue to maintain a presence in Italy in the corporate finance field.
Once the world's largest bank outside Japan, Credit Lyonnais intends to limit its retail banking to France and focus on wholesale and capital market operations elsewhere.
The bank announced last April it was planning to sell its stake in Creberg.
